assumptions.choice: Automatic Elliott Wave counting is inherently subjective; implemented as a deterministic zigzag-pivot state machine that validates the classic non-overlap/alternation rules plus the spec's named Fibonacci checks (wave3=161.8% of wave1, wave4=61.8% retrace of wave3, within a 35% tolerance band) rather than true discretionary wave analysis.
assumptions.reason: infeasible: canonical EW counting requires human judgment; the closest literal reading is a rule-based approximation using the exact ratios the spec names

assumptions.choice: Swing highs/lows detected via a symmetric 5-bar fractal (confirmed 5 bars after the pivot bar).
assumptions.reason: spec does not specify a pivot/fractal window; a fixed, declared parameter is required for any deterministic wave/pattern engine

assumptions.choice: 3% price tolerance for 'roughly equal' shoulders/tops/bottoms, 2% minimum pattern height/depth, 20-bar volume MA with 1.2x breakout confirmation multiplier.
assumptions.reason: spec requires 'standard confirmation criteria (volume, neckline breakout, minimum depth/height)' but gives no numeric thresholds

assumptions.choice: Flag and Pennant are detected with one combined consolidation-after-pole detector (10-bar pole with >=8% move, 5-bar tight consolidation <=50% of pole range) rather than two distinct geometric detectors.
assumptions.reason: spec lists them as separate patterns with the same underlying definition (pole + brief consolidation, continuation breakout); distinguishing parallel-channel vs converging-triangle consolidation shape is not specified

assumptions.choice: 3-wave corrective (ABC) structures are named in the spec's indicator description but the entry/exit rules only reference impulse completion and 'start of a new 5-wave structure', so no separate ABC detector gates trading decisions.
assumptions.reason: the stated entry/exit conditions never reference a corrective-wave trigger directly; adding one would be an invented extra filter not stated in the rules

assumptions.choice: 'Start of a new 5-wave structure' (used to exit an open position) is detected as the first fresh pivot breaking beyond the prior same-type pivot in the opposite direction (i.e., a confirmed lower low after a high for bearish, or higher high after a low for bullish).
assumptions.reason: spec gives no operational definition of 'start' short of a full new impulse; using the same pivot machinery as the impulse detector keeps this literal and consistent

assumptions.choice: The 'key support/resistance level opposite to the open position' is the pattern's neckline; a post-entry close back through it (support break for longs, resistance break for shorts) triggers exit.
assumptions.reason: the spec names support/resistance in this exit clause without defining the level; the neckline is the only level already established at entry and 'broken resistance becomes support' is standard technical-analysis practice for this exact level

assumptions.choice: Stop-loss is placed just beyond (0.2% buffer) the more extreme of (a) the pattern's extreme point (head/trough/peak) and (b) the completed impulse wave-5 extreme, satisfying the spec's 'beyond the nearest local high/low or beyond the extreme of the chart pattern.'
assumptions.reason: spec offers two alternative reference points via 'or' with no tie-break rule; using the more conservative (further) of the two guarantees the stop is beyond both stated references

assumptions.choice: Position size is computed as floor(2% of current portfolio value / per-share stop distance); trade is skipped if this computes to 0 shares.
assumptions.reason: the spec explicitly requires stop-loss risk to be capped at 2% of account balance per trade, which is a stated sizing rule and therefore overrides the canonical default of unsized buy()/sell()

assumptions.choice: 161.8% (not 127.2%) of pattern height, added to/subtracted from the neckline, is used as the sole take-profit target.
assumptions.reason: spec lists both '127.2% or 161.8%' as examples without specifying which applies when; 161.8% is chosen for consistency with the spec's own emphasis on 161.8% as the primary Elliott Fibonacci extension ratio (used for wave 3)

assumptions.choice: At most one open position at a time; no new entries while a position (long or short) is open.
assumptions.reason: canonical default; spec does not state otherwise

assumptions.choice: Both long and short entries are implemented via plain buy()/sell().
assumptions.reason: spec explicitly defines a 'Short position (Sell)' entry rule, overriding the canonical long-only default
